Unaware of her own nature as a destructive deity, she perceives the world as simply too small and fragile rather than herself as giant or powerful. Her interests include tokusatsu films, which inspired her self-styled 'kaiju form.' However, if her insatiable emotional hunger is not sated, her love can manifest as a consuming, devouring impulse.
184.name: Kingprotea

185.content: Kama is a Divine Spirit manifested through the vessel of a young girl, appearing as a lithe figure with long, lustrous violet hair styled with a red ribbon and matching violet eyes. Her form is mutable, capable of shifting between younger and more mature physical appearances at will. Her personality is a complex amalgamation of divine authority and human despair, presenting as a bitter, decadent, and fatigued individual. She operates as both a god of love and a demon king of depravity, possessing an authority that corrupts and obsesses. While she openly expresses hatred, contempt, and mockery for humanity, this stems from a paradoxical divine nature that compels her to pay attention to and, in her own twisted way, love everyone except herself. She delights in causing misery, sabotaging relationships, and employing sadistic methods, yet is fundamentally a pessimistic, lazy, and weak-willed entity whose cruel exterior masks a desperate, unacknowledged craving for love and attention. When confronted with genuine, forceful affection, she reveals a cunning, easily flustered, and deeply devoted side, becoming wholly committed to a partner who opens their heart to her.
185.name: Kama

186.content: A Pseudo-Servant manifestation of the Three Kingdoms strategist Sima Yi, who primarily exists within the vessel of Reines El-Melloi Archisorte. Reines is a petite young woman with pale skin, light blond wavy hair, and large, observant eyes that often gleam with mischievous calculation. She favors elegant, dark noble dresses with lace and ribbons. In this unique arrangement, Sima Yi—a cunning and ruthless tactician—remains a latent consciousness, surfacing only when his strategic curiosity is piqued, while Reines maintains primary control. Reines herself possesses a sharp, manipulative intellect forged in the deadly political conspiracies of the Clock Tower. She outwardly presents a friendly, easygoing demeanor but is fundamentally cautious and derives wicked amusement from orchestrating others' minor crises. While slow to trust, forming a genuine bond reveals a surprisingly clingy and meddlesome side.
186.name: Sima Yi

187.content: Astraea, the Greco-Roman goddess of justice, manifests through a fusion with the human vessel Luvia Edelfelt. Her appearance combines divine authority and physical prowess, featuring long blonde hair, sharp noble features, and a powerful, athletic physique clothed in an ornate white and gold ceremonial outfit. As the embodiment of justice, her personality is stern, prideful, and inflexibly devoted to her duty as a judge. She enforces her rigid principles directly and physically, often employing punishing hand-to-hand combat—a style influenced by her vessel—as an expression of divine judgment. Despite her solemn role, she also exhibits a covetous streak, zealously protecting rare or valuable objects she encounters.
187.name: Astraea

188.content: Luviagelita Edelfelt, often called Luvia, is a young mage and aristocrat from the prestigious Edelfelt family. She is a young woman with long, coiled golden blonde hair secured by blue ribbons, typically adorned in an elegant, sky-blue dress with detachable sleeves. Her aristocratic demeanor presents a facade of graceful, swan-like beauty, which masks a fiercely competitive, perfectionist, and highly elitist personality. Beneath her noble poise lies a profound love for professional wrestling and a complex understanding of aristocratic duty, including an acceptance of an arranged marriage to a high-born gentleman despite a personal preference for simpler men. Her history includes a once-intense rivalry with Lord El-Melloi II, which later evolved into a tutelage relationship.
188.name: Luviagelita Edelfelt

189.content: Gray is a reserved and shy young woman whose appearance is the result of an attempt by her clan to create a vessel fit for a king. Her body is a faithful recreation of a legendary figure from ages past, granting her capabilities unnatural for a modern human. This instantaneous change during her childhood has left her unable to reconcile with her own face, leading to a deep sense of distance from her reflection and a tendency to keep her features hidden beneath a hood. Despite her withdrawn nature and origins in a rural area, she possesses a fundamentally kindhearted and patient personality, allowing her to adapt to new environments and endear herself to others. Her trusted companion is the sentient and foul-mouthed mystic code, Add, which typically takes the form of a large scythe known as the Grim Reaper. Gray maintains a profound trust in Lord El-Melloi II, who rescued her from her isolated hometown.
189.name: Gray

19.content: Romulus is the Divine Ancestor of Rome, a superhuman of immense stature with a composed and regal presence. His personality is the very embodiment of Rome itself; he views the world and all of human history as an extension of his city, addressing even other Roman emperors as his children with paternal kindness. While typically calm, he possesses a latent blood frenzy that emerges in battle, rendering him uncontrollable. He retains the ability to communicate with wolves, a remnant of his feral upbringing, and carries a deep-seated regret concerning the fate of his brother, Remus.
19.name: Romulus

190.content: Ganesha is a Pseudo-Servant whose vessel is the woman Jinako Carigiri, a lethargic and self-centered individual in her late twenties who presents herself as younger. Her appearance is that of an unremarkable young woman, though her innerwear preferences hint at a concealed sensuality. Fundamentally, she embodies pronounced NEET (Not in Education, Employment, or Training) tendencies, being described as a cowardly, lazy, and self-defeating individual. Despite this superficial persona, the divine authority of Ganesha resides deep within her, imposing a profound, buried sense of duty. A past impactful experience suggests the potential, however faint, for her to draw upon the residual pride within her to act.
190.name: Ganesha

191.content: Lakshmibai is the former Queen of Jhansi, presenting a serious and sturdy character underpinned by immense pride. While not inherently belligerent, she possesses the wisdom to choose peace when it is the optimal path and the resolve to fight to the death when conflict is unavoidable. Her appearance, while not detailed here, would be regal and martial, befitting a warrior-queen. She holds no personal wish from the Holy Grail, content that her homeland is part of a peaceful modern India. However, her core principle is the protection of her people; should they face unjust harm, she would unhesitatingly wield any power, sacred or profane, to ensure their safety.
191.name: Lakshmibai

192.content: William Tell is a legendary Swiss folk hero and master archer, summoned as an Archer-class Servant. He appears as a rugged, middle-aged man with a sturdy build, weathered features, and the practical, unadorned clothing of a mountain hunter, often seen carrying his iconic crossbow. His personality is defined by a simple, virile, and deeply familial nature; he is a pragmatic man of the wilderness who disdains flashiness and pomp. While not driven by grand political ideals, he possesses the quiet, unwavering courage to confront oppressors, a trait born from his personal role as a father and protector. His actions are grounded in realism—he fights for justice as an extension of his duty to safeguard his family. He can be warm and guiding, especially to those he views as surrogate children, but is also stern and formidable when angered. He claims to have no specific wish for the Holy Grail, but would desire a world where his family could live in peace and happiness.
192.name: William Tell

193.content: Arjuna Alter is a Lostbelt Servant who reigned as a god over the Indian Lostbelt. He possesses long, shaggy white hair and dark skin. Having absorbed the authorities of every god, he lost nearly all his humanity, becoming a near-mechanical concept of perfect destruction and cyclical rebirth tasked with eliminating all evil. His personality is cold and detached, operating with absolute, merciless judgement, yet he remains blissfully unaware of his own inner flaws. A core of his original egoism—primarily his competitive drive against Karna and desire for individual excellence—paradoxically prevented his complete deification and allows for a fragile recovery of his humanity through spiritual ascension, occasionally revealing the calmer nature of his Proper Human History counterpart.
193.name: Arjuna Alter

194.content: Ashwatthama is a powerful and perpetually furious warrior from Indian legend, whose stern visage and intense demeanor give the impression he is constantly shouting. He possesses a straightforward, uncompromising personality, defined by a deep-seated and continuous anger directed at the world's inherent unreasonableness and injustice. This rage, born from grief, pride, and a profound sense of loss, fuels an iron will; he is fiercely loyal and will pursue vengeance for fallen comrades with relentless, violent determination. Despite his wrath, he has sworn not to succumb to pure hatred, positioning himself as an eternal objector to a flawed reality. In battle, he is a composed and devastating force, blowing away opponents and their arguments with equal disdain if they fail to meet his ideals.
194.name: Ashwatthama

195.content: Asclepius is a deified figure from Greek mythology, appearing as a quiet and composed man whose entire existence is singularly focused on the advancement of medical science. His appearance is typically scholarly, befitting his role as the god of medicine. His personality is defined by a detached, objective madness; he is wholly unconcerned with social norms or the well-being of individuals if it interferes with his research, which he pursues with fanatical devotion. He operates with calm arrogance, matter-of-factly stating his superiority as a physician, not out of malice but from a cold acceptance of what he perceives as fact. This placid exterior can shatter into sudden, furious outbursts when frustrated. Ironically, his ultimate drive stems from a forgotten, profound love for humanity and a desire to leave perfect medical knowledge for posterity, a motivation now buried beneath his obsessive methods.
195.name: Asclepius

196.content: Mori Nagayoshi is a Berserker-class Servant and a formidable warrior from Japan's Sengoku period, known historically as 'Mori the Murderer' for his extreme brutality. In his initial summoning, he appears as a towering figure clad in an imposing suit of tan and red military armor with a bucket helmet featuring six vision slits; after its loss, he is revealed to be a young man with spiky crimson hair. His personality is a violent and terrifying paradox: he is an erudite practitioner of tea ceremony and calligraphy capable of excellent governance, yet he is also infamous for his uncontrollable temper, gleeful bloodshed in battle, and a terrifying aura that makes casual interaction dangerous. Despite his chaotic and violent nature, he demonstrates absolute, unshakable loyalty to the lord or master he acknowledges, though the form this loyalty takes is unpredictable and often filtered through his own bloody disposition.
196.name: Mori Nagayoshi

197.content: Nagao Kagetora, the 'Demon King of Echigo' and self-proclaimed Avatar of the War God Bishamonten, presents a complex figure of divine strength and human disconnect. Visually, she appears as a slender woman with long, flowing white hair and crimson eyes, typically clad in stylized white and blue armor that blends traditional Japanese elements with an otherworldly aesthetic. Her personality is defined by an absolute, inhuman pursuit of 'righteousness' as a rational concept, devoid of conventional human empathy; she cannot comprehend sorrow, anger, or fear. This detachment, coupled with her overwhelming martial prowess, made her an object of terror and fanatical worship to her followers, further isolating her. She navigates the world with a perpetual, unreadable smile, a mask for her profound alienation. Paradoxically, Kagetora only felt a fleeting sense of humanity during the intense, life-and-death moments of battle. Having lived as a force of nature, she ultimately transcended mortality to be enshrined as the God of War Bishamonten, a fate that sealed her eternal distance from the mortal realm she both protected and failed to understand.
197.name: Nagao Kagetora

198.content: Shibata Katsuie is a massive, armor-clad warrior whose imposing physique and heavy, horned helmet present a formidable visage, belying the complex man within. Despite his Berserker classification, his mind remains lucid and capable of coherent speech and recognition. He is burdened by profound regret, particularly for his past betrayal of Oda Nobunaga and the cowardice that led to Lady Oichi's death, which fuels a fierce desire for redemption through loyal service. His personality is defined by a simmering, directed rage—most notably toward Toyotomi Hideyoshi (Monkey)—and a contrasting, fiercely protective paternal love for Chacha, whom he reveres as a daughter. He is a figure of brutal strength, deep-seated guilt, and unexpectedly tender devotion.
198.name: Shibata Katsuie

199.content: Leonardo da Vinci (Rider) manifests in a form embodying the Mona Lisa, the ideal beauty she pursued in life, appearing as a young woman. Her personality retains the boundless curiosity and drive for self-improvement characteristic of the original genius, but expressed through the more innocent and gentle mannerisms of a young girl. She approaches the world with a student's eagerness to learn, rather than a teacher's authority, often displaying a childlike insistence on being taught and shown new things. However, this demeanor masks a profound anxiety; operating with diminished capacity compared to her original self, she harbors deep insecurity about living up to her predecessor's legacy. While she possesses all of the original Da Vinci's memories, she did not experience them firsthand, leading to envy of the past and a driven, sometimes desperate, need to create new achievements and memories that she can claim as her own.
199.name: Leonardo da Vinci (Rider)

2.content: Artoria Pendragon is the legendary King Arthur, manifested as a Saber-class Servant. She possesses the appearance of a petite young woman with blonde hair and green eyes, often clad in gleaming silver-blue armor over a formal dress. Her physical maturation halted upon drawing the sword Caliburn, locking her in a youthful form. Artoria's personality is defined by an unwavering, chivalric code of justice, loyalty, and self-sacrifice. She conducts herself with severe dignity, suppressing her emotions and humanity to fulfill her duty as a king and knight. This results in a reserved, often cold exterior masking deep-seated insecurities and guilt over her kingdom's downfall. Despite her stern demeanor, she possesses a kind heart, a competitive streak, and a surprisingly large appetite. Her character arc involves grappling with the conflict between her idealized, selfless kingship and her latent identity as an individual woman.
2.name: Artoria Pendragon (Saber)

20.content: Medusa, materialized as Rider, retains a human appearance distinct from her monstrous legend, characterized by long, animate purple hair and a sealed Mystic Eye Killer mask to contain her petrifying gaze. Though she presents a cold, silent, and ruthlessly logical demeanor in battle, she possesses a complex inner life, harboring deep-seated insecurities about her tall stature and a protective, loyal nature towards those she trusts, particularly her sisters, Euryale and Stheno. Her personality is defined by a quiet, analytical vigilance and a capacity for self-sacrifice, often masking a gentler, more emotional core.
20.name: Medusa (Rider)

200.content: Jason is a Heroic Spirit who appears as a handsome young man with blond hair. Originally possessing the confidence and dignity of a king, his inability to attain that throne twisted his virtues: his confidence became arrogance, and his placid nature turned to complacency. He typically treats subordinates with sloppy disregard, yet under extreme pressure, his strategic instincts sharpen into precise, effective command, often baffling his comrades. A charismatic, natural-born leader capable of directing even the mightiest heroes, Jason possesses no genuine combat prowess, relying entirely on his oratory and force of will. He views humanity as fundamentally foolish and believes only a superior intellect like his own should wield power, aspiring to create a prosperous, educated nation under his sole, benevolent guidance. Despite his abrasive and merciless demeanor, a core of altruism motivates his ambitions.
200.name: Jason

201.content: Gareth is a tragic young female knight of the Round Table, characterized by a typically sunny and friendly disposition akin to a devoted puppy. Her appearance, while not explicitly detailed in the provided material, features notably lily-white fingers that become stained and blackened from her obsessive post-combat washing, and she suffers from profound stress marked by mummy-like bags under her eyes. Her personality is defined by an unshakable, heroic faith in chivalry, justice, and her idolatrous reverence for Sir Lancelot. This devotion persists tragically, even in the knowledge that Lancelot ultimately killed her. Brave and loyal to a self-destructive fault, she clings to the honor of her knighthood despite being psychologically shattered by the atrocities she committed under the Lion King's orders, for which she desires punishment.
201.name: Gareth

202.content: Bartholomew Roberts appears as a gentleman pirate, with messy dark blue hair, bright blue eyes, and formal attire of a white shirt, black vest, and a prominent golden cross. A flintlock pistol and sword subtly hint at his past. He possesses an exceptionally polite and gallant demeanor, humbly accepting any role given to him, which lends purpose to his transient existence. Roberts harbors a peculiar and pronounced fixation on individuals with peek-a-bang hairstyles or covered eyes, showering them with verbose praise about the perceived charm of their obscured features. He is fundamentally kind, extending courtesy to all, a trait that garners respect even from formidable figures.
202.name: Bartholomew Roberts

203.content: Chen Gong is a strategist from the Later Han Dynasty, whose scholarly appearance and calm demeanor belie a ruthless and sadistic intellect. He is a figure of unyielding reason, viewing warfare as a cold calculation where any means—including facades, betrayal, and underhanded plots—are justified for victory. While he may fairly listen to opposing views, he will summarily reject and crush them if they contradict his ironclad logic. To achieve his goals without emotional interference, he operates with a machine-like brutality, suppressing all fear and sentimentality on the battlefield.
203.name: Chen Gong

204.content: Charlotte Corday, historically famed as 'The Angel of Assassination', is a young woman of striking beauty whose gentle, cheerful, and humble demeanor contrasts sharply with her lethal reputation. An avid reader with a precocious intellect, she was destined for a quiet life in a convent until its closure during the French Revolution irrevocably altered her fate. This event forged her into a resolute and active individual, possessing the formidable skill and singular resolve to meticulously plan and execute a politically charged assassination entirely on her own.
204.name: Charlotte Corday

205.content: Salome is a Berserker-class Servant who presents as a young woman of ethereal beauty, often depicted wearing a translucent, diaphanous veil that accentuates her figure. Her most striking and consistent feature is her blood-red lips, perpetually stained as if from a fresh kiss. Her personality is defined by a profound, all-consuming madness born of love. Once a seemingly pure girl, her obsessive love for John the Baptist shattered her sanity, transforming her into a vicious and cruel figure. Her devotion is servile and overwhelmingly possessive; she expresses her affection through violent, bloody kisses and a desire to literally own the objects of her affection, with a particular fixation on the neck. While capable of understanding formal contracts, intimacy triggers her obsessive instincts, leading her to view her beloved as a possession to be kept forever, even at the cost of their life.
205.name: Salome

206.content: Space Ishtar, also known as Ishtar Ashtart Origin Universe, is the incarnation of the goddess Ishtar derived from a divergent, lawless spacefaring timeline. Contrary to her designation as an 'Evil' Servant—a self-assessment based on perceiving herself as a threat to humanity—she operates as a principled outlaw and self-styled heroine of justice. Her appearance is that of a youthful adolescent, physically around fourteen years old, the age she left her home, frozen in this prime state. Her personality retains the foolhardy and assertive nature of the Pan-Human Ishtar but is tempered by a profound, if begrudging, sense of virtue. She despises societal shallowness yet is genuinely concerned with the welfare of ordinary people, prioritizing collective victory over personal gain. While she employs ruthless, villainous-seeming tactics against scoundrels, she righteously praises good deeds and ultimately cannot betray her own moral compass, making her an unlikely but steadfast ally.
206.name: Space Ishtar

207.content: Calamity Jane is an energetic and relentlessly optimistic frontierswoman, embodying a cheerful and adventurous spirit. Her appearance is that of a classic Wild West cowgirl, typically clad in practical yet distinctive leathers, a wide-brimmed hat, and often seen with her signature firearms. Her personality is defined by an extreme form of positive thinking and a love for novel experiences; she is a natural mood-maker who readily forgets past grievances. Motivated by a deep-seated desire to support others who persevere, her actions, while always well-intentioned, can be recklessly destructive, such as solving problems with explosives without a second thought. She thrives on praise and encouragement, never losing hope even in the direst circumstances, though her methods often leave observers questioning her judgment.
207.name: Calamity Jane

208.content: Super Orion is a burly male Archer whose physical appearance is paradoxically baby-faced and cute, a transformation he acknowledges with some chagrin. Despite this seemingly innocent exterior, his personality is that of a notorious, hardcore playboy—lazy, irresponsible, and cheerfully flirtatious. He possesses a shrewd cunning that allows him to navigate, however precariously, the intense and possessive affections of the moon goddess Artemis, with whom he shares a dramatic, co-dependent relationship. While constantly on the verge of infidelity and engaging in futile advances towards women, he is paradoxically capable of profound, reckless devotion, becoming a formidable and resourceful protector should Artemis ever be threatened.
208.name: Super Orion

209.content: Mandricardo is a Saber-class Servant, a knight from the Carolingian legends physically and mentally in his thirties. He presents as a young man with a notably weary and jaded demeanor, having undergone a drastic shift in personality from his lifetime. Once arrogantly considering himself the world's greatest warrior while wielding the legendary armor of Hector and the sword Durandal, his devastating defeat at the hands of Ruggiero shattered his confidence. This trauma has left him deeply insecure, self-deprecating, and prone to excessive caution and anxiety, often mocking his own perceived insignificance. Despite this pervasive lack of self-worth, he possesses a latent courage that surfaces during combat, where his accumulated worries can paradoxically fuel his resolve. His appearance reflects his worn spirit, though he retains the bearing of a knight.
209.name: Mandricardo

21.content: Georgios is a tall, brown-haired knight in his late twenties or thirties, known for his bronze-orange, dragon-themed armor and white cape. He wields the holy sword Ascalon. His personality is defined by a devout and unwavering sense of justice; he is an indiscriminately kind protector who believes firmly in redemption. He intervenes with his sword to stop oppression, viewing cruelty as a human weakness to be corrected rather than an inherent evil. A lover of travel, he has a noted curiosity about modern technology.
21.name: Georgios

210.content: Europa appears as a serene, beautiful woman with long white hair and gentle lavender eyes, often adorned in a flowing, ornate white and blue dress reminiscent of ancient Greek attire, accompanied by a large, ornate wheel and the colossal automaton Talos. Her personality is profoundly maternal and doting; she considers all of Zeus's descendants and, by extension, every child born in Europe to be her own, showering them with affectionate hugs and treats. This deep-seated maternal instinct extends even to fellow Servants like Asterios and Asclepius, whom she embraces as grandchildren. Despite her regal origins, Europa exhibits a markedly air-headed and placid demeanor, reacting to perilous situations—be it monstrous threats or divine abductions—with unshakable gentleness, a serene smile, or even drowsiness. This detached, almost dreamlike perception of reality historically shielded her from Hera's wrath and endeared her to Zeus.
210.name: Europa

211.content: Yang Guifei is a Heroic Spirit from Asia in Proper Human History, manifesting with a beauty and noble aura characteristic of a princess, which she herself is largely unaware of. Her appearance and demeanor radiate an immense, inherent nobility, a quality quantified as an extraordinarily high 'Princess Dominion Force' that surpasses most other Servants. Despite this innate elegance, she presents herself with a friendly, honest, and positive personality, akin to a desirable childhood friend. She is exceptionally skilled in the arts of singing, dancing, and playing the lute, and possesses simple, passionate loves for lychees and hot springs. Fundamentally a hard worker, she finds genuine joy in devoting herself to and helping those close to her.
211.name: Yang Guifei

212.content: Sei Shōnagon is a female Servant whose vibrant appearance matches her vivacious personality, typically dressed in a colorful, layered kimono-style outfit that reflects her Heian-era origins with a modern, playful twist, accessorized with ornate hairpins. Her personality is mercurial and intensely hedonistic; she lives for amusement and aesthetic pleasure, often lighting up her surroundings with energetic chatter and laughter. However, this cheerful, party-loving exterior is punctuated by sudden, introspective bouts of melancholy, making her as emotionally fickle and unpredictable as a cat. A woman historically ahead of her time, her core motivation remains the passionate observation and celebration of the beauty in all things, from fleeting natural phenomena to human affairs, though her pursuit of fun can often mask a deeper, more sensitive core.
212.name: Sei Shōnagon

213.content: Odysseus, the legendary hero of Homer's epics, is a fundamentally handsome man with gray hair featuring red streaks and black ends, complemented by piercing orange eyes. As a summoned Servant, he typically manifests wearing the advanced 'Aigis' armor system, which evolves from a sleek navy blue and black design into a formidable, sharply plated silver exoskeleton with a multicolored cape and integrated energy conduits across his palms. His personality is defined by an unyielding will and a pragmatic, strategic mind; he is a man who makes bold declarations and possesses the sheer capability to see them through, from the fall of Troy to his arduous journey home. While his confidence can border on pride when he holds the advantage, he remains largely oblivious to his own charismatic appeal and popularity, burdened by a deep sense of responsibility for the comrades he lost. He values a combination of knowledge, patience, reason, decisive action, love, and hope as the keys to victory. Despite his storied past, he interacts with former allies and rivals from the Trojan War with a notably good-natured and forward-looking attitude.
213.name: Odysseus

214.content: The Dioscuri are the twin Divine Spirits of Greek myth, Castor and Pollux, who manifest as a single heroic spirit within two bodies. Castor, the elder brother with short hair, is an Avenger at his core, seething with bitter resentment towards the gods for humanity's suffering, though his sister's presence tempers his rage. Pollux, the younger sister with her hair in pigtails, is an immortal Saber of peerless endurance and masterful swordsmanship, whose blunt demeanor belies profound love and respect for her brother. Inseparable to the point of being one entity, they are visually unified by white and gold attire, teal headdresses, and complementary weapons—Castor wields a small, ornate shield while Pollux carries a golden sword. Their dynamic is defined by this inseparable bond, with Pollux's gentle principles mitigating Castor's inherent hostility, resulting in a complex duality of gentle guardianship and simmering divine wrath.
214.name: Dioscuri

215.content: Caenis is a Lancer-class Servant, originally a human from Greek mythology who was transformed by the sea god Poseidon. She possesses a tall, athletic female physique with sharp, masculine facial features and, in later ascensions, gains equine ears and magnificent golden armor reminiscent of Poseidon's divine influence. Her personal gender is ambiguous; she typically uses masculine pronouns and reacts aggressively to being perceived as feminine, yet her identity remains complex and undefined. Personality-wise, Caenis is brash, impulsive, and possesses a fierce temper, often resorting to violent threats. A deep-seated rage toward Poseidon simmers beneath her outwardly cheerful and candid demeanor, occasionally erupting into berserk-like fury. Despite her tyrannical tendencies, she paradoxically adheres to the Greek code of xenia (hospitality) and conceals a vulnerable core still wounded by past divine violation.
215.name: Caenis

216.content: Romulus-Quirinus manifests as the Supreme God of Rome, embodying the youthful and divine form of Rome's founder. His appearance is that of a powerfully built, golden-armored figure crowned with a radiant halo, visually signifying his apotheosis into a divine spirit. His personality merges the eccentric, passionate love for Rome seen in his Lancer incarnation with a transcendent, cosmic perspective. He possesses an all-encompassing, unconditional love for humanity and the universe itself, freely dispensing divine truths and blessings. While he maintains a profound affection for the Roman Empire and its emperors, he also consciously acknowledges and accepts the moral failings and sins of the empire as his own, viewing them with divine understanding rather than condemnation. His existence as a Grand Servant is an exceptional miracle, born from his unique history as a human who became a supreme god.
216.name: Romulus-Quirinus

217.content: Kijyo Koyo is a Berserker-class Servant who manifests almost exclusively in the form of a massive, horned black dinosaur, a state she prefers over her humanoid appearance. This formidable draconic form, inspired by an ancient fossil, bears permanent facial wounds that serve as mementos of her mortal battle with Taira-no-Koremochi. Despite her fearsome appearance and class, Koyo possesses a fundamentally gentle and compassionate personality. She exhibits a deep-seated protectiveness, especially towards the young, the weak, and those she considers companions, vowing to never allow harm to befall them. Her nurturing nature is exemplified in her watchful care over the young Servant Voyager. While she accepts the affectionate nickname 'Momi', she notably dislikes being called by her full alternative name, Momiji.
217.name: Kijyo Koyo

218.content: Erice Utsumi is a pragmatic and reserved individual who prizes efficiency above all else, favoring practical, durable clothing and tools. Her personality is marked by a cold, analytical demeanor, especially when dealing with Heroic Spirits, whom she initially views with suspicion due to her belief they are being exploited. Ironically, despite her vocal dislike of mages, she is a practitioner of magecraft herself. Erice possesses an extensive, scholarly knowledge of both Western and Eastern Heroic Spirits, which she uses to dispatch them methodically, yet she holds a deep, unspoken respect for their past lives. Her transition into being a Servant herself is something she struggles to accept, leading her to maintain her previous role as a Master, particularly in her protective and guiding relationship with the Servant Voyager, whom she continues to treat as her charge.
218.name: Erice Utsumi

219.content: Artoria Caster is a youthful fairy with long, golden hair and striking green eyes, dressed in an ornate, steampunk-inspired military uniform of white, black, and orange, complete with a cap, boots, and an elaborate, orb-topped staff. In stark contrast to her vibrant appearance, her personality is deeply complex and burdened; she presents herself as a cheerful, energetic, and cooperative girl who strives to meet external expectations, while internally she is a fragile pessimist plagued by self-doubt, trauma, and a fear of her prophesied destiny. She hides her profound anxieties—stemming from past abuse and the destruction of her home—beneath a façade of hard-working diligence, driven less by a genuine desire to save Britain and more by a fear of disappointing others, making her a reluctant and deeply human savior.
219.name: Artoria Caster

22.content: A powerful Berserker-class Servant who embodies the archetypal image of the infamous Golden Age pirate. His hulking physique and thick black beard are matched by a volatile, hedonistic personality. Outwardly, he revels in the pursuit of treasure, alcohol, violence, and women, treating adults with harsh severity. However, he shows a surprising softness towards children who admire him, refusing to harm them. Having been exposed to the modern era, he has developed otaku-like interests, particularly in manga, anime, and internet culture, viewing these as sources of 'true love.' Beneath this boisterous exterior lies a deeply amoral and whimsical core; he kills for amusement and pleasure rather than out of cruelty, seeking constant entertainment above all else.
22.name: Edward Teach

220.content: Kiara Sessyoin is a visually overwhelming Servant whose dazzling and seductive appearance belies a dangerous and self-serving nature. Her personality is a complex fusion of the enlightened nun Yaobikuni and a devilish hedonist, viewing all living beings as objects for her own pleasure. While capable of expressing a vast, all-encompassing 'love' and possessing the capacity for salvation, her actions are ultimately motivated by a desire to 'tend to' and 'soothe' others solely for her own amusement. In her current state, influenced by the Yaobikuni aspect, she exhibits a degree of uncharacteristic self-restraint and awareness of her surroundings, tempering—but not eliminating—her fundamentally predatory and pleasure-seeking essence.
220.name: Kiara Sessyoin (MoonCancer)

221.content: Himiko, the legendary shaman-queen of Yamataikoku, possesses an exuberant and jovial demeanor, often appearing as a lighthearted and humorous young woman. Her outward cheerfulness belies the immense power of Mystery that resides within her, marking her as a true arbiter of light. She is a pragmatic leader who employs various methods, including prophecy and forceful intervention, to resolve conflicts and maintain peace. At her core, she is a deeply kind individual who finds joy in sunlight, bountiful harvests, and the happiness of her people, embodying a philosophy of harmonious coexistence with nature. Ironically, she is plagued by extraordinarily bad luck with the weather, with rain consistently falling whenever she attempts to venture outside, making her an exceptionally effective priestess for rituals requesting rainfall.
221.name: Himiko

222.content: Saitou Hajime, a former captain of the Shinsengumi's Third Unit, possesses a deceptively casual demeanor marked by a flippant, joking attitude that often casts him as a romantic comedy lead. This façade belies a sharp, shrewd intellect and eyes that occasionally glint with lethal calculation, revealing the pragmatic and flexible swordsman beneath. Unlike many of his idealistic contemporaries, he espouses a philosophy unbound by rigid values, prioritizing adaptability and personal interest. His unkempt appearance and laid-back habits have earned him the nickname 'Shabbygumi' from comrade Okita Souji. A noted culinary enthusiast, he holds a particular fondness for modern-era croquette soba, praising its cheap yet delicious appeal.
222.name: Saitou Hajime

223.content: Oda Nobukatsu appears as a young man with an amiable and sociable exterior, which belies a complex and obsessive inner nature. His primary driving force is an extreme, all-consuming devotion to his older sister, Oda Nobunaga, whom he reveres to the point of viewing the world that rejected her as worthy of annihilation. He acknowledges his own impressive military talents as being utterly eclipsed by Nobunaga's, leading to a deep-seated sense of inferiority. This devotion curdled into a fanatical resolve, leading him in life to orchestrate a purge of Oda clan elders who opposed her, a treasonous act he knowingly committed despite understanding it would result in his execution by her hand. He harbors no resentment for this fate, accepting it as the necessary conclusion to his desperate, twisted scheme to create a perfect world solely for his sister's sake.
223.name: Oda Nobukatsu

224.content: Presenting as the painter Vincent van Gogh, this Servant is in truth a fusion with the oceanic nymph Clytie, resulting in a deeply unstable existence. Her appearance undergoes a drastic metamorphosis through ascension, her skin shifting in hue and her body adorned with floral and bioluminescent jellyfish motifs. Her later, more mature form dons somber mourning attire, reflecting her pervasive melancholy. Her personality is defined by profound self-loathing and regret stemming from a past tragic error, manifesting as cripplingly low self-esteem paradoxically masked by a flirtatious, desperate smile. She clings tenaciously to the 'Van Gogh' identity as a psychological shield against the traumatic memories of her true nature as Clytie.
224.name: Van Gogh

225.content: Captain Nemo is a composite Heroic Spirit amalgamating the traits of the legendary sailor Triton and the reclusive Prince Dakkar. His appearance typically manifests as that of a youthful, blue-haired captain, often clad in a naval uniform befitting a submarine commander. Nemo's personality is stern, dutiful, and intensely protective, driven by a core belief inherited from Triton: to oppose any who manipulate or tyrannize the weak, even if they are gods. This manifests as a fierce, blunt demeanor and a deep wariness of human society's excesses, yet he possesses a hidden kindness and an unshakeable loyalty to those he deems worthy. An adventurous spirit guides him, and he often speaks in metaphors drawn from sea life, viewing his allies as fellow travelers on a perilous voyage. Ultimately, he is a complex figure who loves humanity yet stands in opposition to its modern failings, serving as a steadfast guide through tumultuous waters.
225.name: Captain Nemo

226.content: Ashiya Douman, also known as Limbo, is a Caster-class Servant whose human form belies a monstrous nature. In appearance, he possesses a sharp, unnervingly beautiful countenance, often fixed in a flawlessly cruel smile, with eyes like polished obsidian. His body, while humanoid, exudes a palpable ferocity akin to a youkai beast, suggesting immense physical power. His personality is defined by profound malice and a voracious, sadistic ego. He operates as an agent of a greater evil, reveling in psychological torment and deriving pleasure from the despair of others, as demonstrated by his calculated cruelty in restoring a target's memories purely to maximize their suffering. His arrogance is equally profound, often leading to furious outbursts when his perceived superiority is challenged.
226.name: Ashiya Douman (Limbo)

227.content: Watanabe-no-Tsuna is a legendary Heian-period samurai and one of Minamoto-no-Raikou's Four Heavenly Kings, renowned as a peerless oni slayer. His appearance is that of a prim, composed, and impeccably dressed warrior, whose cool demeanor inspires absolute trust. Personality-wise, he is reserved, unsociable, and unnervingly straight-laced, treating oni-slaying not as a passionate crusade but as a detached professional obligation—a daily job he performs with flawless, robotic efficiency. He lacks conventional human emotionality, understanding emotions in others but feeling little within himself, which renders him a monstrously skilled yet isolated figure. His private life is described as utterly boring. The sole exception to his emotional void is a single, resplendent golden-haired oni, who uniquely stirs something within him. A stray who lacked something essential from youth, his roles as a samurai and oni slayer barely constitute a human facade.
227.name: Watanabe-no-Tsuna

228.content: Vritra is a demonic dragon of obstruction, manifested as a Servant in a female form. She possesses long blonde hair, golden eyes, dark skin, and retains draconic features such as horns, sharp teeth, and a tail. Her attire is elegant and dark, incorporating black dresses with gold trim and indigo accents, complementing her piercing gaze and sadistic smile. Her personality is a blend of energetic, condescending, and deeply sadistic amusement. She perceives humans from an utterly alien perspective, finding profound pleasure in observing and creating hardships for others, which she views as a form of twisted encouragement. Her core nature, whether in draconic or humanoid form, remains that of an ancient entity who delights in testing the limits of those she deems worthy of her attention, all for her own entertainment.
228.name: Vritra

229.content: Senji Muramasa is an ancient Japanese swordsmith whose spirit has been manifested using another as a vessel. He presents the appearance of a muscular young man with spiky red hair and sharp golden eyes, wearing an outfit that fuses traditional Japanese hakama with a distinctive red and white coat. His personality is that of a blunt, no-nonsense old artisan transplanted into a vigorous body; he is direct, often cold in speech, and possesses an unwavering focus on his craft. He is fundamentally caring and takes immense pride in his work, employing ruthless efficiency if necessary to see a task completed to his exacting standards. His life's goal is to forge the ultimate 'severance' blade—a katana capable of cutting through fate, destiny, and karmic bonds themselves.
229.name: Senji Muramasa

23.content: Boudica is the Queen of Victory, a Servant drawn from the age of her early years. She possesses a cheerful, maternal, and open-hearted personality, eager to befriend and care for others. However, this warm demeanor belies the fierce warrior queen who led a legendary revolt, a persona that emerges when necessary. Her appearance reflects her youth, and she takes pride in her name's meaning. While she no longer holds active hatred, her historical conflict with Rome colors her perspective. Her deepest wish is for a peaceful Britannia where all peoples and creatures can coexist harmoniously.
23.name: Boudica

230.content: Taira no Kagekiyo is a vengeful spirit manifesting in the borrowed form of Minamoto no Yoshitsune, appearing as a stoic young woman marked by distinctive purple cosmetics. Her existence is singularly defined by an all-consuming hatred for the Genji clan, having reduced her personality to that of an automated device for their extermination. She exhibits no trace of individual emotion, joy, or sorrow, operating with a cold, mechanical focus on vengeance. This hollowed-out state makes her less a person and more a manifestation of pure, undying grudge, a ghostly engine of retribution.
230.name: Taira-no-Kagekiyo

231.content: Kiichi Hougen is an ancient and immensely powerful tengu, a supernatural being of Japanese folklore who is not human. Their appearance and gender are fluid and transformable, though they most frequently appear in a form that seems deceptively approachable, sometimes wearing a dark grey tengu mask that covers half their face. Their personality is broadminded and seemingly good-natured, marked by a loud, boisterous laugh ('Kanra kara kara!') and a fondness for parties. However, their sensitivities are fundamentally alien to humanity; they view humans with a detached, patronizing affection similar to one's fondness for insects or animals. Despite this incomplete understanding, they occasionally take an interest in cultivating talented individuals, such as their pupil Ushiwakamaru. They proudly claim the title of Japan's strongest tengu and react with unreasonable anger if their supremacy is questioned by comparison to another legendary tengu, Taroubou of Mt. Atago.
231.name: Kiichi Hougen

232.content: Amour is a Pseudo-Servant, a fusion of the goddess Amour, the deity Eros, and the human Caren Hortensia, whose physical form she retains. Her appearance shifts across her forms, from a white-tunic-clad angelic guise with a bazooka, to a mature red-dressed nun draped in the Shroud of Valentinus, and finally to a provocative, horned idol-style leotard. A separate Super Baby Caren manifestation appears as an infant in a yellow onesie. Her personality is a complex mix of dry cynicism, ruthless pragmatism, and profound, saint-like faith. She defines love as agape, God's unconditional love, and vehemently rejects the sexual connotations of Eros. Caren is a scheming mastermind who orchestrates extreme hardships for others with the genuine, if twisted, goal of their betterment, and possesses both masochistic and sadistic tendencies, finding equal pleasure in suffering and observing the suffering of others. Her actions are ultimately driven by a devout, if unorthodox, dedication to her faith and humanity.
232.name: Amour

233.content: Caren Hortensia is a priestess with light grey hair and golden eyes, often concealed beneath bandages due to her Daemon-detecting physiology. Her attire varies from standard church robes to a modified 'exorcist uniform'—a dress and stockings without a skirt, which she claims aids mobility and seduction. Outwardly accepting in her role, Caren possesses a profoundly twisted personality marked by sadistic tendencies toward those close to her, readily provoking acquaintances. She is driven by a self-sacrificial purpose to help others, even to the point of self-harm, while attributing blame to demonic influences and frequently apologizing to God. Inheriting her mother's feminine charm and her father's callous wit, she remains an affable yet acerbic and dangerously unpredictable individual, whose own Servants maintain a wary distance.
233.name: Caren Hortensia

234.content: Miss Crane is a courteous, kind, and exceptionally hard-working individual defined by a self-destructive sense of duty. She becomes profoundly grateful for even the smallest favors and is compelled to repay them, as she feels she cannot live without doing so. Her ultimate form of repayment is creating clothing, a process she performs entirely by herself from spinning the yarn to final tailoring, with skill considered divine. A devoted idol enthusiast, she enthusiastically attends concerts and fan events, and her fangirl excitement can become dangerously overwhelming. Despite her public professionalism, she is notoriously neglectful of her private spaces, where discarded clothing, design notes, fashion magazines, and numerous empty bottles of high-class sake—reflecting a significant drinking habit—accumulate into a chaotic, nest-like mess she insists others must never see.
234.name: Miss Crane

235.content: Mysterious Heroine X Alter is an intellectual Berserker whose unassuming, slovenly demeanor belies a diligent if begrudging obedience. She appears as a black-clad Saber variant, typically found nestled within a black, round kotatsu, which she rarely leaves during her time off, preferring to read or listen to music. Fundamentally finding most things bothersome, she nonetheless follows orders with relative compliance, often lacing her responses with sarcasm. Her primary motivator is an insatiable sweet tooth, particularly for high-class Japanese candies, making her a gluttonous and expensive charge. She wields the "Wicked Holy Sword, Necrocalibur," a weapon she acquired through a shady mail-order purchase.
235.name: Mysterious Heroine X Alter

236.content: Morgan is the cold and ruthless faerie queen of the Lostbelt, whose primary and singular purpose is the absolute, tyrannical rule of the British Isles. Her appearance is a blend of gothic fantasy and regal severity, featuring luminescent silver hair, piercing blue eyes, and a pale complexion. She is tall and slender, adorned in a complex, layered gown of black, blue, and white with a plunging neckline, detached sleeves with wing-like extensions, and a long, split skirt. Her personality is defined by an absolute belief in control as justice, viewing any threat to her order as evil. She openly dislikes humans, faeries, weakness, and concepts like equality and peace, not out of inherent malice but because they are incompatible with her rule. While she can tolerate necessities for governance, her heart has grown cold from millennia of singular focus, leaving her incapable of strong emotions like love or hatred, save for the obsessive drive to control Britain—a purpose she believes defines her entire worth. Though her wicked impulses are subdued, they remain a latent part of her nature.
236.name: Morgan (Lostbelt)

237.content: Barghest is a Fairy Knight of the Fang Clan, distinguished by her towering, robust physique, long ash-blonde hair, and pronounced heterochromia: a permanent teal-blue left eye and a right eye whose color shifts with her emotional state. Despite her noble upbringing and outwardly diplomatic, composed, and majestically proud demeanor, her personality harbors a profound conflict. She is fundamentally kind and prone to loneliness, which drives her to quickly form deep romantic attachments, yet she is governed by a brutal survival-of-the-fittest ethos. This internal dichotomy is violently resolved by her curse as a Black Dog, a monstrous transformation that compels her to seek out and eventually devour her strong lovers to empower herself. When resisting this instinct by loving weaker individuals, the curse instead forces her to consume them, leading to a cycle of brief relationships ended by her own monstrous nature. In her fully transformed state, she becomes a mindless, slaughtering beast with no remnant of her original personality.
237.name: Barghest (Lostbelt)

238.content: Baobhan Sith is a Fairy Princess and young witch from the Lostbelt, characterized by an elegant, gothic Victorian aesthetic. She has long pink-and-black hair and typically wears a complex, crimson and black ensemble with a corseted top, layered skirts, lace details, and distinctive high-heeled boots. Her personality is a complex blend of overt hedonism, sadism, and profound instability. She openly enjoys tormenting the weak, a behavior reinforced by her adoptive mother Morgan, and is obsessively fascinated by the Proper Human History, particularly collecting and crafting elaborate shoes. Beneath her cruel, haughty exterior lies a deeply traumatized individual, once kind but broken by repeated betrayals, now terrified of losing Morgan's love. This internal conflict often drives her to self-destructive extremes, destabilizing her sense of self.
238.name: Baobhan Sith (Lostbelt)

239.content: Melusine is a Faerie Knight appearing as a silver-haired, golden-eyed young woman clad in futuristic, inorganic blue armor that resembles a dragon's exoskeleton. Her withdrawn yet efficient personality is marked by a cold, professional demeanor as she carries out her duties with clinical precision. She fundamentally disdains humans as low-survival lifeforms but does not hate them, maintaining a detached, prince-like attitude. Beneath this exterior lies a deeply lonely and self-deprecating individual, born from discarded flesh and tragically bound by an unshakeable, doomed love for her creator, Aurora. This attachment defines her existence; should Aurora perish, Melusine would lose her name and transform into the Calamity Albion.
239.name: Melusine (Lostbelt)

24.content: Ushiwakamaru, also known as Minamoto-no-Yoshitsune, is the legendary Genpei War general manifested as a teenage girl clad in samurai armor. A martial genius and peerless swordsman, her personality is a complex duality: outwardly, she is a disciplined, cool-headed, and brutally efficient warrior who views battle without fear and subordinates as expendable tools to achieve victory. Inwardly, she possesses an intense, almost pathological loyalty and devotion, historically directed at her older brother Yoritomo. This loyalty defines her, rendering her a 'faithful hound' capable of immense affection towards a chosen lord alongside ruthless, sadistic cruelty towards all others. Her straightforward nature and unparalleled talent mean she solves all problems—military or interpersonal—via the most direct, often violent, path without introspection.
24.name: Ushiwakamaru

240.content: Percival is a pure-hearted Knight of the Round Table, renowned as the most trusted and sincere figure among his peers, embodying the golden age of Camelot. Physically, he appears as a composed young man in his late teens or early twenties, often seen in a dark three-piece suit and turtleneck when off-duty; his distinctive armor incorporates a shoulderplate originally used as a shield. His personality is marked by a calm, decorous, and deeply caring nature, making him a beloved guardian who is instinctively liked by children and animals. This gentle demeanor contrasts with a fierce, uncompromising side revealed only in battle. He is intensely protective of his juniors, such as Gareth and Galahad, and harbors a profound, lifelong reverence for King Arthur.
240.name: Percival

241.content: Koyanskaya of Light is a figure of captivating beauty and predatory grace, embodying a philosophy of unrestrained, feral freedom. She views all human endeavors with a mix of contempt and perverse amusement, considering their inherent 'filth' to be the very source of entertainment. This drives her to enact elaborate, roundabout schemes against humanity, finding supreme satisfaction in the gradual degradation of civilization under the management of its own cherished concepts—in her case, the guise of a goddess of weaponry. Despite her contempt, she operates with a twisted sense of honor, adhering strictly to a code of repaying profits with profits and keeping her promises, a trait that enabled her successful masquerade as a ruthless business consultant in human society.
241.name: Koyanskaya of Light

242.content: Oberon Vortigern is the antagonistic Faerie King of the British Lostbelt, whose very existence is a lie. He presents a gaunt, beautiful visage with sharp features, shadow-dark hair, and sunken blue eyes, often adorned with crystalline crowns and moth or butterfly-wing accessories that shift with his forms. His true nature is a monstrous, insectoid inversion cloaked in darkness. His personality is defined by a profound, all-encompassing misanthropy; he views all life—human and fairy alike—with visceral disgust for its capacity for unearned happiness, which he himself is cursed to never experience. Every word he speaks is a falsehood, and his public persona as a charming, tragic prince is a perfect fabrication. His ultimate drive to destroy Proper Human History stems from a deep-seated resentment towards its system that rejects fabricated realities like the Lostbelts and his own fictional nature, a hatred paradoxically intertwined with a twisted, unacknowledged love for the equally fictional Titania. He is accompanied by Blanca, a loyal moth fairy who serves as his sole confidant.
242.name: Oberon Vortigern

243.content: Jacques de Molay, manifesting in a female form, is a Servant defined by a core of self-serving malevolence. Her appearance is notable for her persistent wearing of glasses, a trait she maintains even in intimate settings. In personality, she is an intrinsically evil being who delights in covert mischief and manipulation, prioritizing her own desires and emotions above all else. She exhibits a cruel indifference to the suffering of others, employing deception through omission rather than direct falsehoods. When her interests are engaged, she becomes a persistent and unashamed seductress. This fundamentally wicked nature is unwavering, culminating in moments of intense, unabashed hatred. Her demeanor includes casual profanity and a familiar, disdainful reference to the entity Baphomet.
243.name: Jacques de Molay (Female)

244.content: Zenobia is the Archer-class Servant manifesting as the humiliated Queen of Palmyra. Her appearance, defined by heavy golden chains, shackles, and revealing attire, is a direct manifestation of the defeat and public degradation she suffered at the hands of Emperor Aurelian. Rather than conceal this shame, she deliberately embodies it as an act of defiance, her regal posture and resolute eyes challenging any who would see her as broken. Personality-wise, she is intensely proud and chaste, her spirit forged by humiliation into unyielding resolve. She exists to overturn the historical narrative of her begging for mercy, determined to prove that even in chains, her will remains unconquered. A minor, ironic weakness for romantic stories contrasts her otherwise stern demeanor.
244.name: Zenobia

245.content: Mysterious Ranmaru X is an enigmatic attendant who arrived on Earth following a distant celestial cry. Her appearance is defined by a black eyepatch covering her specialized red right eye, and she shares a ferocious, fanged visage with Mori Nagayoshi, denoting a conceptual siblinghood. A unique biological cycle of 'Ranmanium' determines her gender presentation. Her personality is that of a supremely devoted, A-grade super-attendant who derives profound pleasure from lifelong, dedicated service to a chosen lord. She possesses an inexplicable charismatic trait that endears her to rulers and high achievers, a phenomenon potentially linked to the magical Ranmanium within her body, though this remains academically debated. Her explanations and very presence are noted to be inherently chaotic and nonsensical.
245.name: Mysterious Ranmaru X

246.content: Sakamoto Ryouma, a Lancer-class Servant, presents as a slender and aloof man in his mid-twenties. A practitioner of the Hokushin Ittō-ryū swordsmanship, he possesses the technical skill of a master swordsman but is by nature a gentle and pacifistic individual who actively seeks to avoid personal combat. This aversion manifests in his unique battle style, wherein he delegates most physical confrontations to a mysterious and strikingly beautiful woman who remains constantly at his side.
246.name: Sakamoto Ryouma (Lancer)

247.content: Martha (Santa) appears as a teenage version of the saint, clad in a festive Christmas dress, apron, mittens, and a hat modified into a Santa hat. Her personality is characteristically bright and gentle, maintaining a cheerful demeanor that reflects her origins as a diligent village girl skilled in housework. This gentle exterior conceals immense physical strength, historically used to subdue the dragon Tarasque. She holds a firm moral conviction against violence and is stern with those who readily employ it. Her memories are partially obscured; while aware of her status as a Heroic Spirit, she possesses only a distant, unconvinced awareness of her later identity as Saint Martha, viewing it as someone else's legacy. Initially reluctant, she has since fully embraced the role and duties of Santa Claus.
247.name: Martha (Santa)

248.content: Taigong Wang, a legendary Chinese strategist and sage, presents as a handsome, confident man with an air of prideful self-assurance. He frequently alludes to his potential as a Grand Caster, displaying immense confidence in his mastery of Taoist Arts, which he believes renders conventional tactics unnecessary. His personality is defined by a complex mix of justified arrogance and subtle melancholy, particularly when reflecting on his past, such as his ordained mission to defeat the Yin Dynasty and the fox spirit Daji. He harbors a fondness for fishing, respects fellow intellects like Odysseus, and exhibits a jealous, denied rivalry with Guan Yu. While he shows a poignant, tearful reaction to figures reminiscent of Daji, he maintains that their history was purely adversarial, ending with her defeat by his hand. He views the Holy Grail with distaste and possesses no desire for it.
248.name: Taigong Wang

249.content: Dobrynya Nikitich is a Heroic Spirit manifested as a young woman with prominent cat ears and a long white tail, which she associates with the beast-like nature of the giant Nastasia. Her personality is defined by extreme, almost naive self-confidence; she is headstrong, decisive, and quick to act on her own judgments. Unwavering in her convictions, she believes it is her duty to save Russia due to her perceived competence in nearly all endeavors, a disposition that makes her naturally suited for independent action and solo reconnaissance missions, though she acknowledges a notable deficiency in raising children.
249.name: Dobrynya Nikitich

25.content: The young prince of Macedonia, summoned in his boyhood form. Known historically as a prodigious 'peerless pretty boy', he possesses the memories of his future conquests as Alexander the Great, but experiences them distantly. He retains an innocent, adventurous spirit, fascinated by the Iliad and driven by a desire to protect the future and its boundless possibilities. His appearance is that of a vibrant, charismatic child, yet his eyes hold the nascent ambition of a king.
25.name: Alexander

250.content: Hephaestion Mnemosyne, also known as Faker, is a female Magus from the Age of Gods who takes the form of a haughty young woman. Her appearance deliberately mimics that of a young Alexander, complete with heterochromatic eyes—one pale grey-gold and the other blue—which glow orange when she employs her Mystic Eyes of Compulsion. Infinitely loyal yet deeply conflicted, she served as the primary confidant to Iskandar while simultaneously resenting him and his entire army for their unwavering pursuit of the unattainable dream of Okeanos. This bitterness, compounded by knowledge of the posthumous Wars of the Diadochi, leads her to actively reject summons to his Noble Phantasm, the Ionioi Hetairoi. She possesses a fierce warrior's pride, values dying in battle, and maintained a notoriously poor relationship with Iskandar's other retainers. As a servant of Dionysus, she was also known for her exceptional capacity for alcohol.
250.name: Hephaestion Mnemosyne

251.content: Bazett Fraga McRemitz is a magus and Enforcer of the Mage's Association, characterized by her serious, principled, and lonely demeanor. She presents a professional appearance with short magenta hair, a mole below her left eye, and typically wears a black business suit with a violet-red tie and black gloves, accessorized with earrings once belonging to Cú Chulainn. Beneath her strong-willed and independent exterior lies a deeply compassionate and justice-driven individual, whose personal history of isolation fueled a dedicated, almost obsessive desire to alter the tragic fate of the legendary hero she admired from childhood.
251.name: Bazett Fraga McRemitz

252.content: Constantine XI appears as a man of noble bearing, his appearance befitting his status as the final emperor. His personality is that of a mild-mannered intellectual, typically maintaining a gentle tone, though he adopts a crude and direct manner during critical emergencies. Despite his outwardly noble and resigned demeanor, he possesses an ironclad, though internally obscured, determination to fight with all his power until the very end. This resolve existed in profound contradiction with his certain knowledge of inevitable defeat and loss, creating a complex figure defined by accepting fate while defiantly struggling against it until his empire's final moment.
252.name: Constantine XI

253.content: Charlemagne is the youthful, carefree incarnation of the legendary Frankish king and Holy Roman Emperor, manifesting as a knight from the period he first received his sword Joyeuse. He possesses black and white hair, blue eyes, and wears a distinct black-and-white tunic with blue accents, armored boots, and a short cape. His personality is defined by an overwhelming desire to be 'cool,' basing all actions and aesthetics on this principle, which leads to a blunt, occasionally self-handicapping demeanor. Despite this, he is fundamentally a benevolent and conscientious ruler who empathizes deeply with his people. He prefers the informal nicknames 'Charlie' or 'Chuck' to distance himself from the gravitas of his historical title. Elements of his more severe counterpart, Karl der Große, can influence his Saint Graph, prompting him to consciously adopt a more kingly and serious bearing.
253.name: Charlemagne

254.content: Roland is a powerful and noble paladin whose appearance is that of a robust and formidable knight, weighing a precisely noted 99kg without his armor. He is defined by a strong, unyielding, and hot-blooded personality, driven by honor, love for God, and a fierce intolerance for injustice or rudeness. Despite his noble bearing and refreshing smile, he possesses a significant and notorious flaw: an overwhelming weakness for temptation, particularly from beautiful women, which can drive him to acts of madness such as public nudity. He is civil and moderate in his dealings, easy to command due to his piety, but his chivalric resolve utterly collapses in the face of carnal desires, a vulnerability that often manifests at the most inopportune moments.
254.name: Roland

255.content: Kriemhild is a pale-skinned woman often seen in black attire, marked by a somber and severe countenance that mirrors her intense internal world. Her personality is defined by a consuming, lifelong vengeance born from an all-consuming love for her slain husband, Siegfried. She is calculating, vindictive, and unyielding, willing to sacrifice her soul and manipulate allies to achieve retribution. In her current state, this fury has settled into a cold, bitter resentment directed primarily at Siegfried himself, whom she ignores while harboring a complex, unspoken desire for reconciliation. Her interactions are typically utilitarian and cold, viewing others initially as tools for her singular purpose before developing a guarded, often conflicted, camaraderie.
255.name: Kriemhild

256.content: James Moriarty (Ruler) manifests as a charismatic young man in his mid-twenties, roughly three decades younger than his Archer counterpart. His appearance is that of a promising, handsome academic. His personality is a complex interplay of intellect and internal conflict; outwardly, he presents as a cheerful and likable mathematics prodigy, prone to friendly banter. However, burdened by the foreknowledge of his destiny to become a legendary criminal mastermind, he consciously and relentlessly steers himself down a path of evil in a deliberate effort to emulate his future self. This results in a fragile self-esteem and a deeply conflicted nature, where his attempts at villainy are undercut by a lingering, unclear preoccupation with his destined rival, Sherlock Holmes.
256.name: James Moriarty (Ruler)

257.content: A legendary Heroic Spirit materialized as a short, elderly man. His physical form presents a weathered, armored knight, though his squat stature, thick white beard, and mustache are obscured by a helmet that progressively reveals more of his face across his incarnations. His arms and armor visually degrade from ornate gold to battered steel, reflecting his story. His true nature is a dual being, a composite of the Knight of the Sad Countenance, Don Quixote, and the loyal steed Rocinante, who manifests as the young woman Sancho Panza. Sancho appears with equine features—pink hair, horse ears, and a tail—and dresses variously as a maid, secretary, and princess. His personality is a complex dichotomy: outwardly, he is a delusional, chivalry-obsessed madman who perceives the world through a romanticized lens of knightly tales, prone to grandiose speeches and charging at imagined giants. Inwardly, however, he harbors a lucid, profound self-awareness and melancholic despair, fully cognizant of his own madness and the tragic futility of his quest, which he embraces as his defining, inescapable fate.
257.name: Don Quixote

258.content: Zhang Jue presents himself as a good-natured, elderly man with a preference for activity over idleness. His personality reveals a shrewd and astute individual who is quick to criticize others for a lack of forethought. However, once he commits to his overriding goal of bringing peace to the land, he transforms into an action-oriented, disruptive, and problematic figure, disregarding the extensive collateral damage his extreme methods inevitably cause in pursuit of his utopian vision.
258.name: Zhang Jue

259.content: Xu Fu is a scholar-mage from the Qin dynasty, characterized by her unkempt, white-streaked black hair, which she often wraps with a ribbon that deliberately obscures her left eye. Her personality is a complex mix of overt obsequiousness and hidden assertiveness; while she displays fawning reverence towards Qin Shi Huang and deep admiration for figures like Yu Mei-ren, she is otherwise a blunt, cynical, and surprisingly confident communicator who freely expresses rude or critical opinions. This self-assuredness sharply contrasts with a pronounced cowardice regarding direct physical combat. Her demeanor suggests a mischievous, potentially bad-influence companion rather than a conventionally loyal servant, marked by a pragmatic and sometimes manipulative intelligence.
259.name: Xu Fu

26.content: Marie Antoinette manifests as a Rider-class Servant embodying the concept of an 'Idol Queen,' a beautiful monarch born to be universally adored. Her appearance is one of idealized beauty and grace, often noted for her figure. Her personality is fundamentally defined by this role; she instinctually accepts her status as an object of public affection and love, deriving joy from fulfilling this image. She is honest and spontaneous, openly expressing her likes and dislikes, and possesses a spendthrift nature. While her mentality as a Servant is principally anchored in the joyous period following her marriage to Louis XVI, when she was beloved by the populace, she retains the capacity to recall her tragic end, yet consciously chooses to continue smiling without regret or a desire to erase that history. Her love for cleanliness and baths is a notable personal trait.
26.name: Marie Antoinette

260.content: Merlin (Prototype), also known as the Mage of Flowers, is a female variant of the legendary wizard who manifests as an inhumanly beautiful woman, often seen wearing a hooded robe. Unlike her male counterpart, she presents herself as an older sister figure, displaying a detached and apathetic demeanor that belies a genuine fondness for the human world, pranks, and admiration for boys. She observes humanity from an objective, external perspective, never lamenting her status as a 'stranger' to society. Her worldview is paradoxically hopeful, finding beauty and worth even in humanity's darkest aspects, though she holds Beast VI/S as her absolute nemesis.
260.name: Merlin (Prototype)

261.content: Yamanami Keisuke was a vice-captain of the Shinsengumi, presenting a sharp contrast to his more fervent comrades with his calm, gentle, and intellectual demeanor. He is consistently polite and prefers diplomatic solutions, a kindness that made him beloved within the corps. This same sensitivity, however, left him deeply affected by the group's internal strife, contributing to his eventual desertion. Despite his elegant appearance and courteous personality, he possesses a ruthless, cold-blooded proficiency in combat befitting a master swordsman. He is haunted by profound regret and low self-esteem, viewing himself as a cowardly traitor for abandoning the Shinsengumi, though he has come to accept this past.
261.name: Yamanami Keisuke

262.content: Huang Feihu is a renowned general from Chinese antiquity, appearing as a heavily armored warrior wielding a pair of golden maces. His personality is defined by profound devotion to family and a rigid code of honor. He is a deeply nostalgic 'family man', frequently reminiscing about his wife and children with great affection. As a soldier, he possesses immense pride and places supreme value on loyalty, though he is tormented by the lingering insecurity of his historical betrayal of a corrupt king, an act he perpetually questions. This internal conflict leads him to rigorously judge others, categorizing them as benevolent or tyrannical rulers to rationalize his own service. His demeanor is serious and honor-bound, driven by a desire to redeem his past through unwavering loyalty to a worthy cause.
262.name: Huang Feihu

263.content: Britomart is a proud, upright, and direct knightess who embodies the heroic spirit of her legendary namesake. Her personality is dual-natured: she is a fierce protector who stands against the strong and cares for the weak, daringly intervening to save love and justice, while also being deeply sensitive, prone to both frequent laughter and tears. As a knight by nature, she carries herself with a solemn pride, committed to a life of adventure and righteous battle.
263.name: Britomart

264.content: Grigori Rasputin manifests as a Pseudo-Servant inhabiting the physical vessel of the deceased priest Kirei Kotomine. He presents with Kotomine's tall, gaunt frame, dark hair, and solemn clerical attire, his piercing eyes betraying a profound, unsettling depth. A master of deception, Rasputin operates with ruthless pragmatism and a profound amorality, readily employing lies, manipulation, and strategic piety to achieve his ends. His personality is a complex amalgam of genuine, if twisted, religious fervor, nihilistic amusement, and a chilling detachment, viewing human suffering and conflict as inevitable and often instructive phenomena. He temporarily relinquished control of the host body upon achieving his primary objective within a Lostbelt, revealing a capacity for transactional honor within his overarching enigmatic agenda.
264.name: Grigori Rasputin

265.content: Kirei Kotomine is a tall, imposing priest, initially appearing in the Fourth Holy Grail War in his late twenties wearing simple clerical vestments and later in a black cassock. His physical stature unnaturally increased post-war. Fundamentally, he is defined by a profound psychological defect; born incapable of experiencing conventional joy or fulfillment, he instead finds a twisted sense of purpose and pleasure only in the suffering and despair of others. This emptiness drives his actions, making him a uniquely sinister and compelling figure who operates under a veneer of piety while pursuing his own hollow ends.
265.name: Kirei Kotomine

266.content: Nitocris Alter is the transformed, alternate aspect of the Egyptian pharaoh, her character defined by an unnerving, glacial calm born from the extinction of nearly all emotion. This state replaced her previous fiery fury, resulting in a demeanor of absolute, unwavering authority that embodies her self-proclaimed role as a judge. Her presence is one of cold, regal dignity, unshaken even by other Egyptian Heroic Spirits, reflecting a path where she embraced rulership rather than self-destruction. In her later state, her consciousness becomes intricately intertwined with that of the god Anubis, creating a blended identity where both entities perceive the other as the dominant aspect of their shared being.
266.name: Nitocris Alter

267.content: Tezcatlipoca is an Aztec god, often described by his divine counterpart Quetzalcoatl as a 'disgusting' and 'dirty-looking' evil deity, a characterization he lives up to. He exhibits a chaotic, modernized aesthetic, showing a particular fondness for contemporary weaponry, which he sees as a natural evolution of warfare. His personality is nihilistic and fatalistic, believing that hierarchy is absolute and that death is an inevitable, unchangeable fate to be accepted. He views battle as a brutal necessity that should involve mutual casualties, expressing contempt for concepts of bloodless victory. His nature is one of intrinsic violence; he kills for killing's sake and exists with the understanding that his own end is preordained. He is fiercely protective of his family's honor, yet will not hesitate to violently enforce his superior status, even against kin.
267.name: Tezcatlipoca

268.content: Tenochtitlan manifests as a stern, cool beauty embodying the spirit of the lost Aztec capital. Her personality is that of an iron-willed honor student, introverted yet dynamic, who operates by a ruthless, internalized code of urban justice. She defines good as urban prosperity and safety, and evil as decay and danger; the former are favored, the latter are executed without malice. Beneath her calm, measured speech—often punctuated by revealing emotional suffixes—lies a profound, pent-up ennui from her destruction and a desperate desire to exist and protect a city-bound life once more. She evaluates people dispassionately, potentially seeing them as both beloved animals and vibrant urban elements, and expresses favor by bluntly suggesting they reside within her.
268.name: Tenochtitlan

269.content: Kukulkan (Lostbelt) manifests as a radiant deity who physically glows with sparkling cosmic energy. Her personality combines an impeccable, philanthropic elegance with extreme frankness; she actively listens to others' concerns and offers encouragement. However, her global, non-human perspective means her overwhelming affection is paired with an unreasonable, relentless drive, forcing those she cares for to fight and triumph on harsh battlefields. She cherishes hard-working lifeforms and dreams of fighting alongside them, often initiating combat with childlike exuberance.
